Subject: Node uplift contingency for late-stage TitanWorks - internal availability sweep

Team —

TitanWorks pushed the timeline up a week in yesterday's sync; they want our committed Dedicated pool to start onboarding a small pilot (3 sustained pods) by mid-June. Legal and finance are green on terms but procurement has asked for a firm node-availability confirmation and a short contingency plan if we hit thermal/slot constraints.

Can we run a quick availability sweep and confirm:
- Exact GPU SKU counts we can guarantee (per region) for the June 10–30 window
- Minimal fallback model (quantized variant or lower-slice) that we could route to automatically if we can't provision full pods
- Estimated impact on latency SLOs for TitanWorks' 2x burst windows

I've attached the last snapshot we shared with them — please update with the internal node mapping (where we'd stage their pods) and a short runbook for a 48-hour uplift (who does what).

Need this back by EOD Thursday PT so I can feed it into procurement and Alex's team.

Thanks —
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Sales — Dedicated
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, dev.patel@redwood.ai, olga.petrov@redwood.ai, hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 29 May 2029 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Node uplift contingency for late-stage TitanWorks - internal availability sweep

Marcus —

Quick pass from infra/ops:

Summary (short)
- We can commit 24 A100-80GB equivalents in us-west for the June 10–30 window without impacting existing reservations. That maps to 3 production pods (8 GPUs/pod with 1 spare per pod) if we slice at 8/GPU per pod.
- Risk window: June 13–16 when a scheduled fleet maintenance is planned — we can move the maintenance back or shift non-critical staging jobs, but that requires a written exception from scheduling (ops/lead).

Fallback options
- Route to an 8-bit quantized variant we host (matches model family) — expected throughput drop ~20% and tail latency +30ms under 95th percentile.
- Alternate region (us-east) has 12 compatible GPUs available but adds ~30–45ms RTT for TitanWorks (network penalty).

Action items (owners)
- dev_patel: provide a node mapping PDF (which racks/slots we would stage) + proposed 48-hour uplift runbook.
- olga_petrov: confirm scheduling exception options and whether maintenance can shift; note any cooling constraints.
- hannah.schmitt: update SLA note for procurement with the latency delta numbers and fallback policy text.

I'll attach the internal node map once dev drops it in.

-karthik
Principal Infrastructure PM

To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Subject: Draft node mapping + 48h uplift runbook (for review)

Attached: node_mapping_v2.pdf — contains:
- Rack list for us-west cluster (rack IDs R-12, R-13, R-14) with slot assignments for TitanWorks pods
- Preflight checklist (image pull, model shard placement, KV warmup steps)
- 48-hour uplift runbook:
  1) Day -2: reserve slice and mark nodes read-only for maintenance blackout
  2) Day -1 morning: push quantized model to canary nodes; run throughput smoke test
  3) Day 0: activate pods (staged in R-12/13/14), enable prefilling of KV cache; monitor P95 for 2 hours
  4) Day +1: ramp to 100% and keep warmers for 24h; if P95 > target, shift traffic to quantized variant and notify account team

Notes:
- Cooling headroom: R-13 has the least margin — avoid scheduling background, noncritical jobs there during uplift.
- Network egress path tested; estimated extra RTT to TitanWorks app in us-west is negligible when colocated.

Pls review and flag anything that needs operations escalation.

-dev

[Attachment: node_mapping_v2.pdf (pdf)]
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@titanworks.io>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, procurement@titanworks.io
Date: Thu, 30 May 2029 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Node uplift contingency for late-stage TitanWorks - internal availability sweep

Marcus / team —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the detailed runbook. Procurement wants two small clarifications before we sign the SOW:

1) If maintenance cannot be shifted (June 13–16), can you commit to the quantized fallback automatically and include an explicit notification SLA (we need to know within 60 minutes of failover)
2) Can you include a short paragraph in the SOW about where our data (metrics, logs) will be stored and retention for 90 days — security is asking for it.

If you can confirm those two items in writing, we can accept the timeline and proceed to signature.

Best,
Alex Mercer
Head of Platform Engineering
TitanWorks
